note: ADR-0298 §3 debt baseline. Two maps, both SHRINK-ONLY — the gate fails on anything NEW. `instanceScopePresence` records DECLARED owners that register from a constructor or a mount function, so the isolation audit cannot prove that their absence at runtime is clean. It is EMPTY as of L-712: all five declared owners now register as import side effects, checked by gate D6, so absence is provable and the runtime presence check has nothing left to catch. A future owner that registers from a constructor must be listed here again. `undeclaredStateCandidates` records files holding module-level project-scoped state with NO declared owner, found by the heuristic sweep in check-declared-project-scopes.ts. That list is the point of the exercise: every entry is a subsystem that could carry Project A's state into Project B today, and until ADR-0298 none of them was written down anywhere. Entries are triaged, not excused — LEAK-RISK entries need a declared owner; NOT-PROJECT-SCOPED entries need only a rename or a one-line confirmation to be removed.

undeclaredStateCandidates.apps/editor/src/engine/graphQueryBusHand: NOT-PROJECT-SCOPED (2026-08-12) — the sweep matched `const PENDING = new Map(...)`, the request-id-keyed result handoff for the three read-only graph verbs (`PENDING` word-matches the heuristic's `pending`). It is a per-dispatch correlation buffer, not project state: `dispatchGraphQuery` mints a fresh rid, dispatches, then reads AND deletes the entry on the very next line of the same awaited call, so the map is empty at rest and holds nothing keyed by project, element or level. A project switch has nothing to clear — there is no entry to leak unless `bus.executeCommand` throws AFTER the handler ran, and such an orphan is rid-keyed garbage no reader can reach (a bounded-memory nit, not a cross-project disclosure). The module's other column-0 state, `_ridCounter`, is a monotonic counter with no project content. This entry stops covering the file if the handoff ever grows entries that OUTLIVE a dispatch (e.g. a subscription or streaming result); that state would need a declared owner. Closes when CommandBus grows a typed return channel for read verbs and the handoff map is deleted.

undeclaredStateCandidates.apps/editor/src/ui/ai/floorplan-import/F: NOT-PROJECT-SCOPED (2026-08-11, W1-3) — `aiAvailabilityCache` memoizes ONE fact: whether this DEPLOY has an AI upstream configured at all (`GET /api/health` reports `features.anthropic = !!(CF_WORKER_URL || ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)`, server.js). That is an environment-variable fact about the running server, not a fact about a project. Switching Project A -> Project B cannot change it, so carrying the memo across a switch is CORRECT, not a leak, and resetting it on switch would only add a redundant health round-trip. The sweep flags it because the identifier ends in `cache`, which is in PROJECT_WORDS — a heuristic word-match, not a scope finding. This entry is a TRIAGE CLASSIFICATION, not a debt raise: there is no leak here to pay down. If FPTiers.ts ever gains state derived from the OPEN PROJECT (a per-project tier plan, a cached page raster, a scale), that state needs a declared owner and this note stops covering the file.

note2026-08-12-D7-PAID: `duplicateScopeNames` is now EMPTY, and that is a PAYMENT, not a blinding. All four entries (`doorStore`, `doorSystemTypeStore`, `windowStore`, `windowSystemTypeStore`) named the same defect: packages/core-app-model/src/stores/{Door,Window}{Store,Types,SystemTypeStore}.ts were STALE FORKS of the live @pryzm/geometry-door / -window stores, each registering a scopeName the geometry copy also registered, so which instance ClearProjectCommand.clearAll() actually cleared was decided by module-evaluation order rather than design. All six files are DELETED as of 2026-08-12; the tombstone with the full reasoning is in packages/core-app-model/src/stores/index.ts (§TOMBSTONE-HOSTED-STORE-FORK). The blocker this file recorded — 'blocked on that file also exporting the DoorStore CLASS through the core barrel, so it is a package-API decision' — was measured and dissolved: NOTHING in the repo imported any of the sixteen symbols the forks exported, from the classes to the Zod schemas to the *TypeCategory unions. Proven by the compiler, not by grep alone: `tsc -p packages/core-app-model` reports an identical 447 pre-existing errors before and after the deletion, none naming a deleted symbol. Re-pointing the barrel at the geometry singletons was REJECTED because @pryzm/geometry-door depends on @pryzm/core-app-model, so a re-export here would close a package cycle. This also strikes the two S3 entries from tools/rac-conformance/certification/gates/authoritative-state-ledger.json (C70 A-INV-1, one kind one store). A fifth duplicate scopeName now fails CI against an empty set, which is the correct end state.
